notes: Fee from the Vermont Judiciary guide 200-00130A dated 07/2025. Act 60 (effective July 1, 2025) narrowed expungement and widened sealing. Requesting your own criminal record check carries separate fees that are not part of the petition. No official processing time for petitions was found.

main_process: record sealing (automatic sealing and petition for sealing); expungement for non-convictions
court_fee: No fee. Virginia law (§ 19.2-392.12:1) says no court fees or costs are charged to file a sealing petition, and as of July 1, 2026 there is also no fee to file an expungement petition.
fee_waiver: Not needed for filing: sealing petitions are free by statute and expungement petitions are free as of July 1, 2026.
free_automatic: Yes. Since Virginia's sealing laws took effect July 1, 2026, certain misdemeanor convictions (such as petit larceny, shoplifting, trespassing, disorderly conduct) are sealed automatically after 7 years with no new convictions, possession-of-marijuana charges and convictions are sealed automatically, and many misdemeanor acquittals and dismissals are sealed automatically, with no petition or fee. Felony acquittals/dismissals can be sealed at case conclusion on the defendant's verbal request if the prosecutor agrees.
summary: In Virginia, there is no court fee to file a petition to seal a criminal record, and since July 1, 2026 there is also no fee to file a petition to expunge charges that did not lead to a conviction. Under the state's sealing law that took effect July 1, 2026, many minor misdemeanor convictions, marijuana possession records and misdemeanor dismissals or acquittals are sealed automatically at no cost.
notes: Sealed records still require payment of any fines, costs or restitution owed. Petition sealing has a lifetime limit of 2 granted petitions. Getting your own criminal record for a petition is free per the Crime Commission; an advocacy source mentioned a $15 State Police record fee and notary costs, likely outdated. Automatic sealing of older records may be rolled out in phases; no official processing time was found.

main_process: vacating a conviction (motion/petition to vacate record of conviction)
court_fee: Generally no filing fee for the motion to vacate, which is filed in the existing criminal case; local practice varies (e.g., Kitsap County District Court charges no fee; a search excerpt reported a $73 fee at Chelan County District Court, not verified). Clerks charge for certified copies of the signed order.
summary: In Washington, people usually ask the court that convicted them to vacate the conviction, and courts generally do not charge a filing fee for that motion, though a few local courts may. Expect small costs for certified copies of the signed order and for any criminal history report you order from the State Patrol.
notes: No statewide official fee statement found. 'No fee' is confirmed on Kitsap County District Court instructions (revised 08/09/2024) and in Northwest Justice Project's felony guide (reviewed April 11, 2025), which says the superior court clerk should not charge a fee. Some local courts may charge (Chelan County District Court reportedly $73; page could not be loaded). Washington has no general automatic clean-slate law confirmed in this research. A secondary site mentions fee waivers under RCW 36.18.022 and GR 34, not verified on an official page. NJP says the process can take many weeks but gives no official timeline.

main_process: petition for expungement of criminal records (W. Va. Code §§ 61-11-25, 61-11-26, 61-11-26a)
court_fee: The same fee as filing a civil action in circuit court (W. Va. Code § 59-1-11(a)(1)), collected in advance by the circuit clerk; about $200 based on the 2014 enacted amendment.

other_fees.item: West Virginia State Police records division fee for processing the expungement order (W. Va. Code § 61-11-26(n)); waived for petitions under § 61-11-26a (treatment/job program route)

fee_waiver: The $100 State Police fee is waived by statute for petitions filed under § 61-11-26a. Secondary sources (Cornell, Legal Aid of West Virginia) say people who cannot afford the filing fee can file a fee waiver affidavit and application with the clerk; this was not confirmed on an official page.
time: If the prosecutor or another served party files a notice of opposition, the petitioner has 10 days after being served with it to reply (per court instructions, W. Va. Code § 61-11-26(e)).
summary: In West Virginia, a petition to expunge a conviction costs the same as filing a civil case in circuit court, which is about $200. If the petition is granted, there is also a $100 State Police processing fee, which is waived for people who qualify through an approved treatment or job program. Expungement there requires a petition and is not automatic.
notes: The official WV code site was unreachable during research, so § 61-11-26 and § 59-1-11 were confirmed only through search excerpts of the official code and the National Reentry Resource Center (CSG Justice Center). The $200 civil filing fee comes from the 2014 enrolled bill SB 458; I could not confirm it is unchanged today, and counties may add costs. Court instructions SCA-C900 are dated 04/01/2021. No automatic expungement law found.

main_process: expungement of court record (ordered by the judge at sentencing under Wis. Stat. § 973.015); removal of arrest information from the state criminal history repository via DOJ
court_fee: No filing fee found in official materials. There is usually no petition: the judge must approve expungement at sentencing, and the clerk expunges the record after the sentence is completed. People sentenced only to a fine or restitution request it with form CR-266.
free_automatic: Partly. If the judge granted expungement at sentencing (generally for people under 25 at the time of an offense with a maximum penalty of 6 years or less), the clerk expunges the court record once the certificate of discharge is received after the sentence is successfully completed, with no further filing. Removing arrest information from the DOJ criminal history repository (for arrests not leading to conviction) has no fee.
summary: In Wisconsin, adult court records can only be expunged if the judge approved it at sentencing, mainly for people under 25 at the time of the offense. The clerk then expunges the record after the sentence is finished, and official guides mention no filing fee for this. Asking the state Department of Justice to remove arrest information for charges that did not lead to a conviction is free.
notes: The Director of State Courts brochure (hosted by Waukesha County) describes the process but does not mention any fee; no official statement of 'no fee' for court expungement was found, and the statute page could not be loaded. Expungement seals only the court record; the DOJ repository keeps convictions. Dismissed or acquitted cases cannot be expunged by the court. DOJ arrest-removal form dated Jan. 2019 states no fee. A pardon does not expunge the record.

main_process: petition for expungement (of arrest records, misdemeanor convictions, or a first felony conviction)
court_fee: $100 per petition for a misdemeanor conviction (W.S. 7-13-1501); $300 per petition for a felony conviction (W.S. 7-13-1502); no filing fee for arrests that did not lead to conviction (W.S. 7-13-1401).
time: Prosecutors and victims have 30 days after service to object to a misdemeanor petition (90 days for a felony petition), and no order can be issued before that period ends (W.S. 7-13-1501(e)-(f), 7-13-1502(e)-(f)).
summary: In Wyoming, it costs $100 to petition to expunge a misdemeanor conviction and $300 for a felony conviction, while there is no filing fee to expunge an arrest that did not lead to a conviction. The court cannot grant a misdemeanor expungement until 30 days after the prosecutor is served, or 90 days for a felony.
notes: Fees confirmed in the 2025 Wyoming Statutes (Article 15). The no-fee rule for non-conviction petitions (7-13-1401) was confirmed via search excerpts of the statute and an Equal Justice Wyoming handout, not a full page read. No fee waiver provision appears in the statute text; none was found elsewhere. A 2021 bill to cut the misdemeanor fee to $50 does not appear to have become law. Getting a DCI criminal history report may carry a separate fee (not confirmed). No automatic expungement law found.
